statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ and $\mathcal{B}$ be additive categories.
Let $F : \mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{B}$ be a functor.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $F$ is additive,
\item $F(A) \oplus F(B) \to F(A \oplus B)$ is an isomorphism for
all $A, B \in \mathcal{A}$, and
\item $F(A \oplus B) \to F(A) \oplus F(B)$  is an isomorphism for
all $A, B \in \mathcal{A}$.
\end{enumerate}
hypotheses: Let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be a functor between additive categories.
conclusions: The following are equivalent: $F$ is additive, the natural map $F(A)\oplus F(B)\to F(A\oplus B)$ is an isomorphism for all $A,B$, and the natural map $F(A\oplus B)\to F(A)\oplus F(B)$ is an isomorphism for all $A,B$.

statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ and $\mathcal{B}$ be abelian categories.
Let $F : \mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{B}$ be a functor.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $F$ is either left or right exact, then it is additive.
\item $F$ is left exact if and only if
for every short exact sequence
$0 \to A \to B \to C \to 0$
the sequence $0 \to F(A) \to F(B) \to F(C)$
is exact.
\item $F$ is right exact if and only if for every short exact sequence
$0 \to A \to B \to C \to 0$
the sequence $F(A) \to F(B) \to F(C) \to 0$
is exact.
\item $F$ is exact if and only if for every short exact sequence
$0 \to A \to B \to C \to 0$
the sequence $0 \to F(A) \to F(B) \to F(C) \to 0$
is exact.
\end{enumerate}
hypotheses: Let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be a functor between abelian categories.
conclusions: Any left exact or right exact $F$ is additive.
$F$ is left exact iff it carries each short exact sequence to a left-exact sequence beginning at zero.
$F$ is right exact iff it carries each short exact sequence to a right-exact sequence ending at zero.
$F$ is exact iff it carries every short exact sequence to a short exact sequence.

statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ and $\mathcal{B}$ be abelian categories.
Let $F : \mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{B}$ be an exact functor.
For every pair of objects $A, B$ of $\mathcal{A}$ the
functor $F$ induces an abelian group homomorphism
$$
\Ext_\mathcal{A}(B, A)
\longrightarrow
\Ext_\mathcal{B}(F(B), F(A))
$$
which maps the extension $E$ to $F(E)$.
hypotheses: Let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be an exact functor between abelian categories.
conclusions: For all $A,B\in\mathcal A$, applying $F$ to short exact extensions yields the specified abelian-group homomorphism $\mathrm{Ext}_{\mathcal A}(B,A)\to\mathrm{Ext}_{\mathcal B}(F(B),F(A))$.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-exact-functor-ext}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ and $\mathcal{B}$ be abelian categories.
Let $F : \mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{B}$ be an exact functor.
For every pair of objects $A, B$ of $\mathcal{A}$ the
functor $F$ induces an abelian group homomorphism
$$
\Ext_\mathcal{A}(B, A)
\longrightarrow
\Ext_\mathcal{B}(F(B), F(A))
$$
which maps the extension $E$ to $F(E)$.

statement:
Let $a : \mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{B}$ and $b : \mathcal{B} \to \mathcal{A}$
be functors. Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{A}$, $\mathcal{B}$ are additive categories,
$a$, $b$ are additive functors, and $a$ is right adjoint to $b$,
\item $\mathcal{B}$ is abelian and $b$ is left exact, and
\item $ba \cong \text{id}_\mathcal{A}$.
\end{enumerate}
Then $\mathcal{A}$ is abelian.
hypotheses: Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be additive categories and $a:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$, $b:\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$ additive functors, with $a$ right adjoint to $b$.
Suppose $\mathcal B$ is abelian, $b$ left exact, and $ba\cong\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal A}$.
